title: Relations and Functions-II
summary: A relation R on a set A is a subset of A × A. R is reflexive if (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A; symmetric if (a, b) ∈ R ⇒ (b, a) ∈ R; transitive if (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R. A relation with all three properties is an equivalence relation (for example equality, similarity of triangles, ad = bc on N × N).
To disprove a property give one counterexample. Example: |x − y| ≤ 2 on Z is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive (1R3, 3R5, but not 1R5).

f is one-one (injective) if f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂; it is onto (surjective) if every element of the codomain has a pre-image. f(x) = x² or x⁴ on R is many-one (f(−1) = f(1)) and not onto (negatives are missed). Linear functions such as 3 − 4x are one-one and onto R.
A graph is a function only if every vertical line meets it at most once — a circle is not a function.
(f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)). Usually f∘g ≠ g∘f. f is invertible exactly when it is one-one and onto; find f⁻¹ by solving y = f(x) for x.
A binary operation * on A is a function from A × A to A. It is commutative if a * b = b * a and associative if (a * b) * c = a * (b * c). Ordinary multiplication on N is both.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (a) If f(x) = (x − 1)/|x − 1|, x ≠ 1, the range of f is ______. (b) If f(x) = 2x³ − 1, then f⁻¹(x) = ______.

True or False: (a) 'is a factor of' on R is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. (b) f(x) = x² + 3 on R is one-one and onto.

(a) True — a | a; a | b, b | c ⇒ a | c; but 2 | 4 while 4 ∤ 2.
(b) False — f(−1) = f(1), and values below 3 are not attained.
objective4: Answer: (a) Is R = {(1,2), (2,1)} on {1, 2, 3} an equivalence relation? (b) Is f(x) = 3 − 4x on R one-one and onto? (c) If f(x) = 2ˣ, find (f∘f)(0). (d) A binary operation on A is a function from ______ to A.

(a) No — (1,1) ∉ R, so it is not reflexive (it is also not transitive: (1,2), (2,1) but no (1,1)).
(b) Yes. One-one: 3 − 4a = 3 − 4b ⇒ a = b. Onto: for any y, x = (3 − y)/4 gives f(x) = y.
(c) f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2 ⇒ (f∘f)(0) = 2.
(d) A × A.
vsa: If A = {1, 2, 3} and R = {(2, 3)}, check whether R is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.

Not reflexive: (1,1) ∉ R.
Not symmetric: (2,3) ∈ R but (3,2) ∉ R.
Transitive: there are no pairs (a,b), (b,c) both in R, so the condition holds vacuously.
Show that the signum function f(x) = 1 (x > 0), 0 (x = 0), −1 (x < 0) on R is neither one-one nor onto.

f(1) = f(2) = 1, so it is not one-one.
Its range is {−1, 0, 1}; for example 2 has no pre-image, so it is not onto.
sa: Show that the relation 'T₁ is similar to T₂' on the set of all triangles is an equivalence relation.

Reflexive: every triangle is similar to itself.
Symmetric: if T₁ ~ T₂ (corresponding angles equal), then T₂ ~ T₁.
Transitive: if T₁ ~ T₂ and T₂ ~ T₃, the angles of T₁ equal those of T₃, so T₁ ~ T₃.
Hence R is an equivalence relation.
Show that (a, b) R (c, d) ⇔ ad = bc is an equivalence relation on N × N.

Reflexive: ab = ba ⇒ (a, b) R (a, b).
Symmetric: ad = bc ⇒ cb = da ⇒ (c, d) R (a, b).
Transitive: ad = bc and cf = de. Multiply: adcf = bcde ⇒ af = be (c, d ≠ 0) ⇒ (a, b) R (e, f).
Hence R is an equivalence relation.
Let f : R⁺ → (−4, ∞), f(x) = x² − 4. Show that f is invertible and find f⁻¹.

One-one: x₁² − 4 = x₂² − 4 ⇒ x₁ = x₂ (both positive).
Onto: for y > −4, x = √(y + 4) > 0 and f(x) = y.
So f is invertible and f⁻¹(y) = √(y + 4).
Show that f : R → R, f(x) = x² − 1 is neither one-one nor onto.

f(1) = f(−1) = 0, so it is not one-one.
x² − 1 ≥ −1 for all x, so −2 has no pre-image: not onto.
